t: What Is Alt Text? Image Descriptions for SEO and Accessibility
d: Alt text describes an image in words for screen readers and search engines. Learn how to write helpful alt text that improves accessibility and image search.
s: Alt Text Written descriptions of images for screen readers and search engines

Alt Text Written descriptions of images for screen readers and search engines Alt Text: A short written description of an image, stored in the page code. Screen readers read it aloud for visitors with low vision, and search engines use it to understand what the image shows.

What Is Alt Text? Alt text, short for alternative text, is a written description of an image added in the page code. Screen readers read it aloud for visitors who are blind or have low vision, browsers show it when an image fails to load, and search engines use it to understand what the image shows. Good alt text describes what matters about the image in the context of the page. Purely decorative images, such as background shapes, use empty alt text so screen readers skip them.
Why Alt Text Matters for Northern Indiana & Michiana Businesses

Why Alt Text Matters for Northern Indiana & Michiana Businesses Accessible websites serve every customer. A Warsaw resident using a screen reader deserves to know that a photo shows "a newly installed walk-in shower with grab bars" just as a sighted visitor does. Accessibility is also part of a professional, trustworthy online presence. Alt text supports SEO too. It helps your project photos appear in Google Images and gives search engines more context about each page, which matters for businesses whose work is visual, such as remodelers, landscapers, salons, and restaurants across Michiana.

How Alt Text Works Describe the content State what the image shows that matters to the reader. Add useful context Include details such as the service or location when they are genuinely relevant. Keep it concise A sentence or short phrase usually works best. Skip "image of" Screen readers already announce images. Leave decorative images empty Use an empty alt attribute for images that add no information.

A Local Example A Middlebury kitchen remodeler's gallery has fifty photos named "IMG_4021.jpg" with no alt text. It adds descriptions such as "white shaker kitchen cabinets with quartz countertops in a Middlebury farmhouse remodel." The gallery becomes usable for screen reader visitors, and several photos begin appearing in Google Images searches for kitchen remodel ideas in Northern Indiana.

Getting Started With Alt Text Audit your most visited pages first: homepage, top service pages, and gallery or portfolio pages. Many website builders show the alt text field when you click an image in the editor, and free accessibility checkers can list every image missing alt text. Write descriptions the way you would explain the photo to someone over the phone. Focus on what the image shows and why it is on the page. Rename new image files with descriptive words before uploading, and make writing alt text part of your routine every time you add a photo, so your site stays accessible as it grows.
Quick Wins to Improve Your Alt Text

Quick Wins to Improve Your Alt Text Add alt text to every meaningful image on key pages Describe project photos with the service and setting Use empty alt text for decorative graphics Rename image files with descriptive words before uploading Describe text inside images, such as logos or charts

What to Watch For Keyword stuffing. Lists of keywords harm accessibility and add no SEO value. Missing context. Describe what matters about the image on that specific page. Image-only text. Important information should also appear as real text on the page. Linked images. When an image is a link, its alt text should describe the destination.

Alt Text FAQ Is alt text required? Alt text is a core part of web accessibility standards such as WCAG, and it is strongly recommended for every meaningful image. How long should alt text be? Usually one short sentence. Complex charts can be summarized in alt text and explained in more detail on the page. Does alt text help SEO? Yes. It helps search engines understand images and supports visibility in image search. What about logos? Use your business name as the alt text for your logo. t: What Is Anchor Text? How Link Words Shape SEO
d: Anchor text is the clickable wording of a link. Learn how descriptive anchor text helps visitors and search engines and which anchor types local businesses use.
s: Anchor Text The clickable words of a link that describe where it leads

Anchor Text The clickable words of a link that describe where it leads Anchor Text: The clickable words in a link. Descriptive anchor text tells readers and search engines what the linked page covers.

What Is Anchor Text? Anchor text is the visible, clickable text of a hyperlink. In the sentence "Learn more about our water heater installation," the words "water heater installation" are the anchor text if they carry the link. Search engines read anchor text as a description of the linked page. Anchors appear both on your own site, through internal links, and on other websites that link to you, through backlinks.
Why Anchor Text Matters for Northern Indiana & Michiana Businesses

Why Anchor Text Matters for Northern Indiana & Michiana Businesses Clear anchor text helps a Goshen homeowner know exactly where a link leads before clicking, which builds trust and keeps them moving toward a call. It also tells Google that your linked page is about that topic, strengthening its relevance for related searches. For local businesses, anchors that mention services and towns, such as "dental implants in Mishawaka," connect your pages to the exact searches your customers make across Michiana.

How Anchor Text Works Descriptive anchors Words that describe the destination, such as "AC repair." Branded anchors Your business name, often used by other sites linking to you. Partial match anchors Phrases that include the topic naturally, such as "tips from our HVAC team." Generic anchors Phrases like "read more" that offer little context. Naked URLs The web address itself used as the link.

A Local Example A Kokomo law firm's blog posts end with "Contact us here" links. It rewrites them to read "talk with a Howard County estate planning attorney" and links each article to the matching practice area page. Visitors click through more often, and the practice area pages gain stronger relevance for estate planning searches in the region. The change also helps visitors using screen readers, who often jump from link to link. Instead of hearing "contact us here" five times, they now hear exactly where each link leads, which makes the site easier for everyone to use.

Getting Started With Anchor Text Review the links inside your blog posts and service pages. Flag any that use vague words such as "click here," "learn more," or "this page," and rewrite them so the linked words describe the destination clearly. Keep the wording natural and varied. Linking to your furnace repair page with "furnace repair," "fix a furnace that will not start," and "heating repair in Elkhart " sounds more natural than repeating one exact phrase. When partners or local organizations link to you, your business name is a perfectly strong anchor, so there is no need to request specific keywords.
Quick Wins to Improve Your Anchor Text

Quick Wins to Improve Your Anchor Text Replace "click here" links with descriptive phrases Name the service or town in links to local pages Vary anchor wording naturally across your site Keep anchors short, usually two to six words Make sure the anchor matches the destination page

What to Watch For Over-optimization. Repeating one exact keyword in many backlinks can look manipulative. Misleading anchors. Anchors should accurately describe where the link goes. Accessibility. Screen reader users often scan links alone, so descriptive anchors help them navigate. Image links. When an image is a link, its alt text acts as the anchor.

Anchor Text FAQ Does anchor text still matter for SEO? Yes. It remains a helpful signal for what a linked page covers, especially for internal links you control. Should I ask other sites to use keywords in links? A business name or natural phrase is usually best. Natural variety reads as more trustworthy. What is exact match anchor text? An anchor that uses the precise keyword a page targets. Use it occasionally among more natural variations. How is anchor text different from alt text? Anchor text is the clickable wording of a text link. Alt text describes an image, and when that image is a link, its alt text serves as the anchor. Does anchor text help accessibility? Yes. Descriptive link text tells every visitor, including those using screen readers, where a link goes. Put It to Work Want every link on your site pulling its weight? t: What Is a Backlink? How Links Build Local Authority
d: A backlink is a link from another website to yours. Learn why quality links matter, which local links help most, and how Northern Indiana businesses earn them.
s: Backlink A link from another website to yours that signals trust

Backlink A link from another website to yours that signals trust Backlink: A link from another website to yours. Links from respected, relevant sources act like votes of confidence and help your pages rank higher.

What Is Backlink? A backlink is a link on another website that points to yours. When the Elkhart County Chamber of Commerce lists your business with a link, or a local news site links to your article, you have earned a backlink. Search engines treat relevant, trusted backlinks as votes of confidence. Google's original ranking system was built on links, and they remain one of the clearest signals of authority, alongside content quality and relevance.
Why Backlink Matters for Northern Indiana & Michiana Businesses

Why Backlink Matters for Northern Indiana & Michiana Businesses For local businesses, a handful of strong local links often matters more than hundreds of random ones. Links from chambers, sponsors, local news, suppliers, and community organizations show Google that your business is part of the Northern Indiana community. Backlinks also send real referral visitors and help AI systems recognize your business as an established entity worth citing.

How Backlink Works Relevance Links from sites related to your industry or town carry the most meaning. Authority Links from established, trusted sites pass more value than links from brand-new or spammy sites. Context The surrounding text and anchor text tell search engines what your page is about. Variety Links from many different domains show broad recognition.

A Local Example A Columbia City brewery sponsors the local 5K, joins the chamber, gets featured in a regional food blog, and is listed by its hop supplier as a customer. Each organization links to the brewery's website. Those four local, relevant links help the brewery outrank a larger chain for "brewery near Fort Wayne " searches. The links also bring real visitors. Runners checking race details click through to the brewery's site, chamber members discover its event space, and readers of the food blog plan weekend visits. Each link keeps working for years after it is earned.

Getting Started With Backlink Start by listing the organizations you already have relationships with: your chamber of commerce, trade associations, suppliers, manufacturers, local charities you support, schools, and community events you sponsor. Many of them have websites with member, sponsor, or dealer pages, and most will happily add a link to your site when you ask. Next, look for local coverage opportunities. Share a story about a community project, a milestone anniversary, or useful local data with regional news outlets and blogs. Create one genuinely helpful resource, such as a seasonal maintenance checklist for Northern Indiana homes, that others want to reference. Track new links in Google Search Console under the Links report, and focus on steady, relevant growth instead of chasing large numbers.
Quick Wins to Improve Your Backlink Profile

Quick Wins to Improve Your Backlink Profile Join your chamber of commerce and industry associations Sponsor local events, teams, and charities that list sponsors Ask suppliers, partners, and manufacturers to list you as a dealer or client Share useful local data or guides that news sites want to reference Claim profiles on reputable local and industry directories

What to Watch For Buying links. Paid links meant to manipulate rankings violate Google's spam policies. Spam networks. Large batches of low-quality links rarely help and can be ignored or penalized. Relevance. A link from a related local site beats a link from an unrelated site overseas. Steady growth. Natural link building grows gradually as your reputation grows.

Backlink FAQ How many backlinks do I need? Quality matters more than quantity. A small business can compete locally with a modest number of relevant, trusted links. Are nofollow links worthless? Nofollow links pass less ranking value but still bring visitors and visibility, and Google may use them as hints. Do links from Facebook or directories count? Social profile links and directory listings usually pass little ranking value on their own, yet they help customers find you and support consistent business information across the web. What is a toxic backlink? A link from a spammy or manipulative source. Google ignores most of these, and serious problems can be addressed with a disavow file. t: What Is a Buyer Persona? Understanding Your Ideal Customer
d: A buyer persona is a research-based profile of your ideal customer. Learn how local businesses build personas and use them to guide messaging and marketing.
s: Buyer Persona A clear, research-based picture of your ideal customer

Buyer Persona A clear, research-based picture of your ideal customer Buyer Persona: A profile of your ideal customer built from real details such as age, location, goals, and common questions. Personas guide the words, images, and channels you choose.

What Is Buyer Persona? A buyer persona is a semi-fictional profile of an ideal customer, built from real research and customer conversations. It describes who they are, what they need, what worries them, how they make decisions, and where they look for information. Most businesses have two to four personas. A home remodeler might have "Growing Family Grace," who needs more space, and "Downsizing Dan," who wants an accessible main-floor living area. Each persona guides different messages and offers.
Why Buyer Persona Matters for Northern Indiana & Michiana Businesses

Why Buyer Persona Matters for Northern Indiana & Michiana Businesses Marketing that speaks to everyone often connects with no one. When a Goshen financial advisor understands that one of its key clients is a business owner planning retirement within ten years, every page, email, and ad can speak to that person's exact concerns. Personas also align your team. Sales, marketing, and customer service share one picture of who they serve, which keeps messages consistent from first ad to final handshake. Personas also make decisions faster. When a new campaign idea comes up, you can ask a simple question, such as "Would Growing Family Grace care about this?", and quickly decide whether it deserves your time and budget.

How Buyer Persona Works Research real customers Interview customers, review sales notes, and study reviews. Find patterns Group shared goals, challenges, questions, and objections. Write the profile Summarize demographics, goals, pain points, and decision factors. Map their journey Note where they search, what they compare, and what convinces them. Apply everywhere Use personas to guide content, ads, offers, and sales conversations.

A Local Example A Warsaw orthopedic clinic interviews patients and finds two main groups: active adults recovering from sports injuries and older adults considering joint replacement. It creates a persona for each. Pages, emails, and ads for active adults focus on getting back to activity quickly, while content for older adults focuses on safety, recovery support, and what to expect. Appointment requests rise because each group finds messages that answer its own questions.

Getting Started With Buyer Persona Talk with five to ten of your best customers. Ask why they chose you, what they worried about before buying, how they searched, and what nearly stopped them. Listen for the words they use, because those words should appear in your marketing. Write a one-page profile for each main customer type with their goals, challenges, questions, objections, and preferred channels. Share it with everyone who writes copy or talks with customers, and review it once a year as your business and market change.
Quick Wins to Improve Your Buyer Personas

Quick Wins to Improve Your Buyer Personas Interview recent customers about why they chose you Use customer language in headlines and ads Create two to four personas, not dozens List each persona's top questions and objections Match offers to each persona's stage and needs

What to Watch For Guesswork. Base personas on real customer research, not assumptions. Stereotypes. Focus on needs and behaviors more than surface demographics. Shelf personas. Use personas actively in planning and copy. Outdated profiles. Refresh personas as your customers evolve.

Buyer Persona FAQ How many buyer personas should I have? Most small businesses do well with two to four personas based on their main customer groups. What is the difference between a persona and a target market? A target market is a broad group. A persona is a detailed profile of a typical customer within that group. Where do I find persona information? Customer interviews, reviews, sales notes, support questions, and analytics all provide valuable details. Do personas help with SEO? Yes. Knowing your customers' questions and language guides the topics and keywords you target. How does Favze use personas? t: What Is a Call to Action? Writing CTAs That Get Results
d: A call to action tells visitors exactly what to do next, such as call, book, or get a quote. Learn how to write and place CTAs that turn visitors into customers.
s: Call to Action (CTA) The clear next step that turns interest into action

Call to Action (CTA) The clear next step that turns interest into action Call to Action (CTA): A button or phrase that invites the visitor to take the next step, such as calling, booking, or requesting a quote. Every important page benefits from one clear CTA.

What Is Call to Action? A call to action, or CTA, is a prompt that invites someone to take a specific next step, such as "Book a Free Consultation," "Get a Quote," "Call Now," or "Download the Guide." CTAs appear as buttons, links, and lines of copy on websites, emails, ads, social posts, and printed materials. A strong CTA is clear, specific, and tied to what the reader wants. It tells people exactly what will happen when they act and why that step helps them.
Why Call to Action Matters for Northern Indiana & Michiana Businesses

Why Call to Action Matters for Northern Indiana & Michiana Businesses Visitors to a local business website usually have a goal: get a price, check availability, or talk to someone. A Mishawaka electrician whose pages end with "Request a Same-Day Estimate" makes that goal easy to reach, while a page with no clear next step leaves visitors to find the phone number on their own. Better CTAs often raise conversions without any increase in traffic, which makes them one of the most cost-effective improvements for Northern Indiana businesses.

How Call to Action Works Start with an action verb Book, call, get, schedule, compare, or download. Name the benefit "Get Your Free Estimate" says more than "Submit." Make it visible Use contrasting buttons placed where people decide. Match the stage Early visitors may want a guide, while ready buyers want to book. Reduce friction Short forms and click-to-call buttons make acting easy.

A Local Example A Goshen tree service's website uses a single "Contact Us" link at the bottom of each page. It adds a "Get a Free Tree Removal Estimate" button near the top of each service page, a click-to-call button on mobile, and a short form asking only for name, phone, and town. Estimate requests increase in the following months with the same website traffic. The company also adds a softer CTA, "See Our Storm Cleanup Checklist," for visitors who are researching rather than ready to call.
Getting Started With Call to Action

Getting Started With Call to Action Review your homepage and top service pages on a phone. Within the first screen, can a visitor see what you offer and one clear next step? If not, add a primary CTA button near the top of each page. Rewrite vague CTAs such as "Submit" or "Learn More" to describe the result, such as "Get My Free Quote." Use one primary CTA per page, repeat it after key sections, and keep forms short. Track clicks and conversions, then test new wording on your highest-traffic page.
Quick Wins to Improve Your Calls to Action

Quick Wins to Improve Your Calls to Action Place a clear CTA button near the top of each key page Use specific, benefit-focused button text Add click-to-call buttons for mobile visitors Shorten forms to only the details you need Offer a softer CTA for early researchers

What to Watch For Too many choices. Several competing CTAs can stall decisions; lead with one. Vague wording. "Submit" and "Click Here" give no reason to act. Mismatch. The page after the click should deliver exactly what the CTA promised. Accessibility. Buttons need readable contrast and large tap targets.

Call to Action FAQ Where should a CTA go on a page? Near the top, after key sections, and at the end, so visitors can act whenever they are ready. How many CTAs should a page have? One primary action, repeated where helpful, with an optional secondary action for early researchers. What makes a CTA effective? A clear action verb, a specific benefit, and an easy next step. What is the difference between a primary and secondary CTA? A primary CTA is the main action you want, such as booking or calling. A secondary CTA offers a lighter step, such as reading a guide, for visitors who are still deciding. Should every email have a CTA? Yes. Each email should guide readers to one clear next step. t: What Is Call Tracking? Connecting Phone Calls to Marketing
d: Call tracking uses unique phone numbers to show which ads, pages, and campaigns make your phone ring. Learn how local businesses use it to measure real leads.
s: Call Tracking Connecting every phone call to the marketing that produced it
Call Tracking Connecting every phone call to the marketing that produced it Call Tracking: A system that uses unique phone numbers to show which ad, page, or listing produced each phone call.

What Is Call Tracking? Call tracking is a method of measuring which marketing efforts produce phone calls. It assigns unique phone numbers to different sources, such as Google Ads, your website, a direct mail piece, or a billboard, so each call is recorded with its source. Dynamic number insertion takes this further on websites, swapping the displayed phone number based on how the visitor arrived. Many tools also record calls, capture caller location, and send call data to Google Ads, Google Analytics, and CRMs such as HubSpot.
Why Call Tracking Matters for Northern Indiana & Michiana Businesses

Why Call Tracking Matters for Northern Indiana & Michiana Businesses For many local businesses, the phone is the main source of new customers. A Goshen family law attorney or an Elkhart garage door company may receive most leads by phone, and without call tracking, those leads look like they came from nowhere. Call tracking shows which channels actually make the phone ring, so budgets shift toward what works. Recorded calls also reveal how well your team handles inquiries and which questions customers ask most.

How Call Tracking Works Unique numbers per source Each campaign or channel gets its own forwarding number. Dynamic number insertion Website visitors see a number tied to how they found you. Calls forward to your line Customers reach your normal phone with no change in experience. Data is recorded Source, time, duration, and location are logged for each call. Integrations share results Calls flow into ad platforms and CRMs as conversions.

A Local Example A Warsaw roofing company runs Google Ads, Facebook ads, and a radio spot, and answers about one hundred calls a month. After adding call tracking with numbers for each channel and dynamic numbers on its website, it learns that most qualified roof replacement calls come from Google search, while radio produces many calls about small repairs. Listening to recorded calls also shows that callers often ask about financing, so the company adds financing details to its website and ads.

Getting Started With Call Tracking List the channels that could produce calls: Google Ads, Local Services Ads, organic search, Google Business Profile, social media ads, print, radio, and signs. Decide which ones you want to measure separately. Choose a call tracking provider that integrates with Google Ads and your CRM, set up dynamic number insertion on your website, and keep your main business number on your Google Business Profile and directory listings for consistency. Review call sources and recordings monthly, and train your team using real call examples.
Quick Wins to Improve Your Call Tracking

Quick Wins to Improve Your Call Tracking Add dynamic number insertion to your website Track calls from Google Ads as conversions Keep your main number consistent on core listings Review recorded calls to improve how leads are handled Send call data into your CRM

What to Watch For NAP consistency. Use tracking numbers carefully so your main business number stays consistent across listings. Recording consent. Follow call recording consent laws and announce recordings where required. Short calls. Set a minimum call duration so wrong numbers do not count as leads. Number ownership. Make sure you can keep tracking numbers if you change vendors.

Call Tracking FAQ Does call tracking hurt local SEO? It does not when set up carefully. Keep your main number on your Google Business Profile and listings, and use dynamic numbers on your website. Can I track calls from my Google Business Profile? Yes. Google Business Profile shows call counts, and UTM parameters on your profile link help track website visits from the profile. Is call recording legal? Rules vary by state, and some states require consent from everyone on the call. Many businesses play a short recording announcement at the start of each call. Check with your attorney for your situation. How much does call tracking cost? Pricing varies by provider and number count, with many small business plans starting at a modest monthly fee. t: What Is a Canonical URL? Preventing Duplicate Content
d: A canonical URL tells search engines which version of a page is the main one. Learn how canonical tags prevent duplicate content and consolidate ranking signals.
s: Canonical URL The preferred version of a page you want search engines to index

Canonical URL The preferred version of a page you want search engines to index Canonical URL: A tag that names the preferred version of a page when similar versions exist, so search engines credit one main address.

What Is Canonical URL? A canonical URL is the main version of a page that you want search engines to index and show in results. It is usually declared with a canonical tag, a short line in the page code that points to the preferred address. Websites often create several addresses for the same content without anyone noticing: versions with and without "www," tracking parameters added by ads or emails, filtered product pages, and printer-friendly copies. The canonical tag tells search engines which one counts.
Why Canonical URL Matters for Northern Indiana & Michiana Businesses

Why Canonical URL Matters for Northern Indiana & Michiana Businesses When search engines find the same content at several addresses, they must guess which to rank, and ranking signals such as links can split between versions. A clear canonical keeps your Elkhart service page's strength focused on one address. Canonical URLs also keep reporting clean. Google Search Console data, analytics, and AI citations all point to the same page, making it easier to measure what each page earns.

How Canonical URL Works One preferred address Choose the URL you want indexed, usually the clean version without parameters. Self-referencing tags Each main page includes a canonical tag pointing to itself. Duplicates point to the original Variations include a canonical tag pointing to the preferred version. Consistent signals Internal links, sitemaps, and redirects all use the canonical address. Google decides Canonicals are strong hints, and Google chooses the final version based on all signals.

A Local Example A Granger furniture store's product pages appear under several addresses because shoppers can sort by color and price. Google indexes many near-identical versions, and none rank well. After adding canonical tags that point each variation to the main product page and updating the sitemap, the main pages become the indexed versions and their rankings improve. Its Search Console reports also become easier to read. Clicks and impressions that were scattered across dozens of filtered addresses now roll up to one page per product, so the owner can finally see which furniture lines attract the most search interest.

Getting Started With Canonical URL Open the Pages report under Indexing in Google Search Console. Look for statuses such as "Duplicate without user-selected canonical" or "Alternate page with proper canonical tag." These tell you where Google sees duplicate versions and which version it chose. Next, confirm that every main page includes a self-referencing canonical tag with the full, final address, including https and your preferred www setting. Most website platforms and SEO plugins add these automatically, so check that the setting is on. Redirect old or alternate versions where possible, and make sure your sitemap and internal links use only canonical addresses.
Quick Wins to Improve Your Canonical Setup

Quick Wins to Improve Your Canonical Setup Add a self-referencing canonical tag to every main page Use one consistent address format with https Point filtered or parameter versions to the main page List only canonical URLs in your sitemap Redirect old page versions to their current address

What to Watch For Conflicting signals. Canonicals that disagree with redirects or sitemaps confuse search engines. Wrong targets. Pointing a page to an unrelated canonical can remove it from search. Relative paths. Use full URLs in canonical tags to avoid mistakes. Redesigns and migrations. Recheck canonical tags after any site rebuild.

Canonical URL FAQ Is a canonical tag the same as a redirect? No. A redirect sends visitors and search engines to a new address. A canonical tag keeps both pages accessible while telling search engines which to index. Do I need canonical tags on a small site? Yes. Even small sites create duplicate addresses through tracking links and platform settings, and self-referencing canonicals prevent confusion. Will Google always follow my canonical? Google treats it as a strong hint. Consistent internal links, sitemaps, and redirects help it agree with your choice. Can I canonicalize to another website? Yes, for syndicated content you publish elsewhere, though the original site should host the main version. Put It to Work Want search engines focused on the right version of every page? t: What Is Conversion Tracking? Measuring Calls, Forms, and Sales
d: Conversion tracking records the actions that matter, such as calls, form fills, and bookings. Learn how local businesses set it up and use it to grow.
s: Conversion Tracking Measuring the calls, forms, and sales your marketing produces

Conversion Tracking Measuring the calls, forms, and sales your marketing produces Conversion Tracking: Setting up your ads and website to record valuable actions, such as calls, forms, and bookings, so you can see what your ad spend produces.

What Is Conversion Tracking? Conversion tracking is the process of recording when a visitor takes a valuable action, such as calling your business, submitting a quote request, booking an appointment, or making a purchase. Each of those actions is called a conversion. Tracking usually runs through tools such as Google Analytics 4, Google Ads conversion tags, Meta Pixel, call tracking software, and your CRM. Together they connect each conversion to the channel, campaign, keyword, or ad that produced it.
Why Conversion Tracking Matters for Northern Indiana & Michiana Businesses

Why Conversion Tracking Matters for Northern Indiana & Michiana Businesses Without conversion tracking, marketing decisions rely on guesses. A Goshen roofing company may know it spent money on Google Ads and Facebook last month, yet not know which one produced the twelve inspection requests. With tracking in place, the answer is clear, and the budget can follow the results. Conversion data also powers modern ad platforms. Google and Meta use conversion signals to find more people likely to take the same action, so accurate tracking directly improves campaign performance for businesses across Northern Indiana and Michiana.

How Conversion Tracking Works Define the actions Decide which actions count: calls, forms, bookings, purchases, chats, or direction requests. Install tracking tags Add Google Analytics 4, Google Ads, and Meta tags, often through Google Tag Manager. Track phone calls Call tracking numbers and Google forwarding numbers record calls from ads and websites. Assign values Give conversions an estimated or actual value so you can measure return. Test and verify Submit test forms and calls to confirm every conversion records correctly.

A Local Example A Mishawaka HVAC company runs Google Ads and Facebook ads and counts leads by asking callers how they heard about the business. After setting up form tracking, call tracking, and Google Ads conversion imports, it learns that most booked furnace replacements come from a handful of search keywords, while a broad Facebook campaign produces mostly low-value inquiries. The company shifts budget toward the strongest keywords and rebuilds the Facebook campaign around a seasonal tune-up offer. Cost per booked job falls, and the owner can finally explain to his partners exactly what each marketing dollar produced.

Getting Started With Conversion Tracking List every way a customer can contact you: phone calls, contact forms, quote forms, chat, booking tools, text messages, and walk-ins. Decide which of those actions count as conversions and which matter most to revenue. Next, set up Google Analytics 4 key events for form submissions and booking confirmations, connect Google Ads conversion tracking, and add call tracking for calls from your website and ads. Test every action yourself and confirm it appears in the reports within a day. Review the data monthly and use it to decide where your next marketing dollar goes.
Quick Wins to Improve Your Conversion Tracking

Quick Wins to Improve Your Conversion Tracking Track form submissions with a thank-you page or confirmation event Add call tracking to your website and ads Import key conversions into Google Ads Assign estimated values to each conversion type Test every conversion after site or form changes

What to Watch For Double counting. Duplicate tags can record one lead twice and inflate results. Missing calls. Phone calls are often the main conversion for local businesses; track them. Privacy and consent. Follow consent requirements and privacy rules when collecting data. Quality versus quantity. Connect leads to sales in your CRM to see which conversions become revenue.

Conversion Tracking FAQ What counts as a conversion? Any action that moves someone toward becoming a customer, such as a call, form fill, booking, purchase, or quote request. Do I need Google Tag Manager? It is not required, but it makes adding and managing tracking tags much easier. Can I track phone calls from Google? Yes. Google Ads call extensions, forwarding numbers, and call tracking tools all record calls. How long does setup take? A basic setup often takes a few hours to a few days, depending on how many forms, phone numbers, and platforms are involved. Put It to Work Want to know exactly which marketing brings in customers? t: What Are Core Web Vitals? Page Speed Metrics Explained
d: Core Web Vitals are Google's measurements of loading, responsiveness, and visual stability. Learn LCP, INP, and CLS, their targets, and how faster sites win more customers.
s: Core Web Vitals Google's measurements of how fast, responsive, and stable your pages feel

Core Web Vitals Google's measurements of how fast, responsive, and stable your pages feel Core Web Vitals: Google's measurements of how fast a page loads, how quickly it responds to taps, and how steady the layout stays while loading. Strong scores create a smoother visit and support better rankings.

What Is Core Web Vitals? Core Web Vitals are three measurements Google uses to describe real visitors' experience on a page. Largest Contentful Paint (LCP) measures loading, Interaction to Next Paint (INP) measures responsiveness to taps and clicks, and Cumulative Layout Shift (CLS) measures how much the layout jumps while loading. Google's "good" thresholds are an LCP of 2.5 seconds or less, an INP of 200 milliseconds or less, and a CLS of 0.1 or less, measured across real visits. These scores appear in Google Search Console and PageSpeed Insights.
Why Core Web Vitals Matters for Northern Indiana & Michiana Businesses

Why Core Web Vitals Matters for Northern Indiana & Michiana Businesses Most local searches happen on phones, often on cellular connections in parking lots or job sites. A Valparaiso customer who waits on a slow page or taps a button that jumps away is likely to go back and choose a faster competitor. Page experience is part of how Google evaluates pages, and fast pages also convert better. Improving Core Web Vitals helps rankings, ad landing pages, and leads at the same time.

How Core Web Vitals Works Largest Contentful Paint How quickly the biggest visible element, often a hero image or headline, finishes loading. Interaction to Next Paint How quickly the page responds visually after a visitor taps, clicks, or types. Cumulative Layout Shift How much content moves unexpectedly as images, fonts, and ads load. Field data Google uses data from real Chrome users over the past 28 days, so improvements show up gradually.

A Local Example A Warsaw boutique's homepage hero image is a 4 MB photo, and its LCP sits around five seconds on phones. After compressing images, serving modern formats, reserving space for the banner, and removing an unused slider script, the page loads in under two seconds and the shop sees more product page visits from mobile searchers.
Getting Started With Core Web Vitals

Getting Started With Core Web Vitals Open Google Search Console and review the Core Web Vitals report for both mobile and desktop. It groups pages as Good, Needs Improvement, or Poor and names the metric holding each group back. Then run your most important pages, usually the homepage and top service pages, through PageSpeed Insights to see specific recommendations. Fix the largest issues first. Oversized images are the most common cause of slow loading, so resize and compress them before anything else. Reserve space for images and banners so content stays steady, and remove scripts or plugins that no longer earn their place. After each round of changes, test on a real phone over a cellular connection, then give Google's field data a few weeks to reflect the improvement before measuring again.
Quick Wins to Improve Your Core Web Vitals

Quick Wins to Improve Your Core Web Vitals Compress images and serve WebP or AVIF formats Set width and height on images and embeds to prevent layout jumps Remove unused scripts, sliders, and plugins Load fonts efficiently and limit font weights Check Search Console's Core Web Vitals report monthly

What to Watch For Field versus lab. PageSpeed lab scores help diagnose, while field data shows what Google uses. Third-party tools. Chat widgets, trackers, and embeds can slow pages; keep only what earns its place. Mobile first. Test on a real phone over cellular, where most local visitors browse. Gradual updates. Field data covers 28 days, so give fixes a few weeks to show.

Core Web Vitals FAQ Do Core Web Vitals affect rankings? They are part of Google's page experience signals. Content relevance matters most, and strong Core Web Vitals help when competing pages are similar. What replaced First Input Delay? Interaction to Next Paint replaced First Input Delay as a Core Web Vital in March 2024. How do I check my scores? Use Google Search Console's Core Web Vitals report for site-wide field data and PageSpeed Insights for individual pages. Put It to Work Want a site that loads fast on every phone in your market? t: What Is Email Deliverability? Reaching the Inbox Every Time
d: Email deliverability is your ability to land in inboxes instead of spam. Learn what shapes it and how local businesses keep their emails reaching customers.
s: Email Deliverability Your ability to land in the inbox instead of spam
Email Deliverability Your ability to land in the inbox instead of spam Email Deliverability: How reliably your emails reach the inbox. Authentication, list quality, and sender reputation shape it.

What Is Email Deliverability? Email deliverability describes how reliably your emails reach subscribers' inboxes rather than spam folders or being blocked. It is different from delivery rate, which only shows whether an email was accepted by the receiving server. Mailbox providers such as Gmail, Yahoo, Outlook, and Apple decide where each email goes based on your sender reputation, domain authentication, engagement, list quality, and content.
Why Email Deliverability Matters for Northern Indiana & Michiana Businesses

Why Email Deliverability Matters for Northern Indiana & Michiana Businesses An email that lands in spam is an email no one reads. For a Goshen retailer announcing a sale or an Elkhart clinic sending appointment reminders, strong deliverability means customers actually see the message. Requirements have grown stricter. Since 2024, Gmail and Yahoo require bulk senders to authenticate their domains, keep spam complaint rates low, and offer easy unsubscribes, and many of those practices help senders of every size.

How Email Deliverability Works Authentication SPF, DKIM, and DMARC prove your emails come from you. Sender reputation Providers track your history of complaints, bounces, and engagement. Engagement Opens, replies, and clicks signal that recipients want your emails. List quality Clean, permission-based lists reduce bounces and spam traps. Content and format Clear, honest messages with working links and a visible unsubscribe link.

A Local Example A Michigan City boutique notices its open rates falling sharply. A review shows its domain lacks DMARC, its list includes years of inactive subscribers, and emails go out from a free email address. After authenticating its domain, sending from its own address, and removing long-inactive subscribers, its emails return to the inbox and sales from email rise. The boutique also starts a quarterly re-engagement email, inviting quiet subscribers to stay on the list or unsubscribe, which keeps engagement strong over time.

Getting Started With Email Deliverability Confirm your domain authentication first. Your email platform will show whether SPF and DKIM are set up, and a free DMARC checker can confirm your DMARC record. Send from an address on your own domain, not a free email account. Next, clean your list. Remove hard bounces, review subscribers who have not opened in many months, and run a re-engagement campaign. Keep an easy unsubscribe link in every email, send consistently, and monitor spam complaints with tools such as Google Postmaster Tools.
Quick Wins to Improve Your Email Deliverability

Quick Wins to Improve Your Email Deliverability Set up SPF, DKIM, and DMARC for your domain Send from an address on your own domain Remove hard bounces and long-inactive subscribers Include a clear unsubscribe link in every email Send consistently instead of in large irregular bursts

What to Watch For Purchased lists. Bought lists damage reputation and violate most platform policies. Spam complaints. Keep complaint rates very low; Gmail asks bulk senders to stay under 0.3%. Sudden volume spikes. Increase sending gradually when your list grows. Broken links and heavy images. Clean, balanced emails perform best.

Email Deliverability FAQ What is a good inbox placement rate? Strong senders reach the inbox for the large majority of their emails. Engagement and authentication drive the result. Why are my emails going to spam? Common reasons include missing authentication, low engagement, old or purchased lists, and high complaint rates. Does sending more email hurt deliverability? Sending more is fine when subscribers want the emails. Sudden spikes and unwanted messages cause problems. Do small lists need to worry about deliverability? Yes. Inbox providers judge every sender, and a small list with strong engagement and proper authentication reaches the inbox reliably, which makes every email count. What is the difference between delivery and deliverability? Delivery means the receiving server accepted the email. Deliverability means it reached the inbox, rather than the spam folder, where the reader will actually see it. How do I check my reputation? Google Postmaster Tools and your email platform's reports show reputation, complaints, and bounce rates. Put It to Work Want every email you send to reach the inbox? t: What Is Double Opt-In? Confirmed Email Subscriptions Explained
d: Double opt-in asks new subscribers to confirm their email address before joining your list. Learn the benefits for deliverability and list quality.
s: Double Opt-In A confirmation step that verifies every new subscriber

Double Opt-In A confirmation step that verifies every new subscriber Double Opt-In: A two-step signup where a new subscriber confirms their email address by clicking a link. It builds a list of people who truly want to hear from you.

What Is Double Opt-In? Double opt-in is a two-step signup process for email or SMS lists. After someone submits their email address, they receive a confirmation message and must click a link (or reply, for text) before they are added to the list. Single opt-in adds subscribers immediately after they fill out the form. Double opt-in adds a confirmation step that verifies the address is real and that the person truly wants to hear from you.
Why Double Opt-In Matters for Northern Indiana & Michiana Businesses

Why Double Opt-In Matters for Northern Indiana & Michiana Businesses A clean list reaches more inboxes. Double opt-in keeps typos, fake addresses, and spam signups off your list, which protects your sender reputation and helps your newsletters land in the inbox for every Northern Indiana subscriber. It also builds a more engaged audience. People who confirm their subscription have shown clear interest, so they tend to open, click, and buy at higher rates, and you have a clear record of consent.

How Double Opt-In Works Signup A visitor enters their email on your form. Confirmation email Your platform sends a message asking them to confirm. Click to confirm The subscriber clicks the confirmation link. Added to the list Only confirmed subscribers receive your campaigns. Welcome message A welcome email sets expectations and delivers any promised offer.

A Local Example A LaGrange County furniture maker collects emails at craft fairs and online. Its list includes many mistyped addresses and some spam signups, and open rates are dropping. It switches to double opt-in for online forms and sends a confirmation email to fair signups. The list shrinks slightly, yet open rates and clicks rise, and fewer emails bounce. The confirmation email also delivers a printable care guide for wood furniture, which gives new subscribers a reason to confirm right away.

Getting Started With Double Opt-In Check your email platform settings for a double opt-in or confirmed opt-in option. Most major platforms, including Mailchimp, Klaviyo, and HubSpot, offer it for forms and lists. Write a short confirmation email with a clear subject line, such as "Please confirm your subscription," a single prominent button, and a note about what subscribers will receive. Update your signup form's thank-you message to tell people to check their inbox. Then track confirmation rates and improve the email if many signups do not confirm.
Quick Wins to Improve Your Opt-In Process

Quick Wins to Improve Your Opt-In Process Turn on double opt-in for website signup forms Write a confirmation email with one clear button Tell signups to check their inbox on the thank-you page Deliver a promised resource after confirmation Remove addresses that never confirm

What to Watch For Lower list growth. Some people will not confirm, which trades quantity for quality. Confirmation in spam. Authenticate your domain so confirmation emails reach inboxes. Clear wording. Make it obvious that a confirmation step is required. SMS rules. Text message programs require clear consent, and confirmation replies are standard.

Double Opt-In FAQ Is double opt-in required by law? In the United States, it is generally not required for email, though some countries and some platforms require or strongly recommend it. It is a strong best practice either way. Does double opt-in reduce my list size? Usually slightly, while improving engagement and deliverability. What confirmation rate is normal? Rates vary, and clear forms and well-written confirmation emails raise them. What should the confirmation email say? Keep it short: thank the person for signing up, explain what they will receive and how often, and give one large button to confirm. A friendly subject line such as "One quick step to join" helps it stand out in the inbox. Should I use double opt-in for SMS? Text marketing programs typically confirm subscriptions with a reply or confirmation message as part of consent best practices. t: What Is a Drip Campaign? Automated Emails That Build Trust
d: A drip campaign is a series of automated emails sent on a schedule or after a trigger. Learn the types of drip campaigns and how local businesses use them.
s: Drip Campaign A series of automated messages sent on a schedule or trigger

Drip Campaign A series of automated messages sent on a schedule or trigger Drip Campaign: A series of pre-written emails or texts that send on a schedule after someone joins a list or takes an action.

What Is Drip Campaign? A drip campaign is a pre-written series of emails, or sometimes text messages, sent automatically over time. Each message is released on a schedule or after a trigger, such as someone joining your list, booking an appointment, or downloading a guide. The name comes from the way messages arrive steadily, a little at a time, instead of all at once. Common examples include welcome series, onboarding sequences, appointment reminders, review requests, and re-engagement campaigns.
Why Drip Campaign Matters for Northern Indiana & Michiana Businesses

Why Drip Campaign Matters for Northern Indiana & Michiana Businesses Small businesses rarely have time to send personal follow-up messages to every contact. A drip campaign lets a Mishawaka med spa welcome every new subscriber, a Goshen accountant remind clients about tax deadlines, and a Warsaw contractor request reviews after each job, all automatically. Because each drip campaign is built once and runs continuously, it delivers consistent communication that keeps your business top of mind and turns one-time contacts into repeat customers.

How Drip Campaign Works Choose a trigger A signup, purchase, appointment, form submission, or date starts the sequence. Plan the messages Map each email's purpose, from welcome to education to offer. Set the timing Space messages days or weeks apart based on the buying cycle. Personalize Use names, interests, and service details to make messages relevant. Measure and refine Track opens, clicks, replies, and conversions for each message.

A Local Example A South Bend dog groomer creates three drip campaigns. New clients receive a welcome series with grooming tips and booking reminders. Every client receives a reminder email six weeks after an appointment, the typical time between grooms. Clients who have not booked in four months receive a friendly check-in with a seasonal offer. The reminder campaign alone fills more of the schedule each month, and the owner spends less time on phone follow-ups.

Getting Started With Drip Campaign Begin with the drip campaign that matches your most common customer moment. For most local businesses, that is a welcome series for new subscribers or a follow-up sequence after a service. Write three to five short messages, each with one purpose and one clear call to action. Set them up in your email platform with sensible spacing, test every link, and send yourself a test run. After a month, review which messages earn the most clicks and replies, and improve the weakest one first.
Quick Wins to Improve Your Drip Campaigns

Quick Wins to Improve Your Drip Campaigns Set up a welcome series for every new subscriber Send service reminders based on typical repeat timing Request reviews automatically after each job Re-engage customers who have been quiet for several months Keep each message focused on one clear action

What to Watch For Set and forget. Review campaigns regularly so offers and details stay current. Overlap. Make sure contacts are not in several sequences at once. Exit rules. Remove people from sales sequences once they buy or book. Deliverability. Authenticate your domain and keep lists clean.

Drip Campaign FAQ How many emails should a drip campaign have? Many effective sequences use three to seven messages, depending on the goal and buying cycle. How often should drip emails send? Welcome series often send every few days, while longer nurture sequences may space messages a week or more apart. Can drip campaigns use text messages? Yes. Many platforms support automated SMS sequences with proper consent. What is the difference between a drip campaign and a newsletter? A newsletter goes to your whole list at the same time. A drip campaign sends each contact a series of messages based on their own trigger, such as the day they signed up or the date of their last service, so timing fits each person. Do drip campaigns work for service businesses? Yes. Reminders, follow-ups, and review requests are some of the most valuable uses. t: What Is E-E-A-T? Experience, Expertise, Authority, and Trust
d: E-E-A-T describes the qualities Google looks for in helpful content. Learn what each letter means and how local businesses show experience and trust on their websites.
s: E-E-A-T Experience, Expertise, Authoritativeness, and Trustworthiness

E-E-A-T Experience, Expertise, Authoritativeness, and Trustworthiness E-E-A-T: Experience, Expertise, Authoritativeness, and Trustworthiness: the qualities Google's quality guidelines use to judge whether content deserves trust. Real credentials, real photos, and genuine reviews strengthen all four.

What Is E-E-A-T? E-E-A-T stands for Experience, Expertise, Authoritativeness, and Trustworthiness. The framework comes from Google's Search Quality Rater Guidelines, which human reviewers use to evaluate whether search results are genuinely helpful. Trust sits at the center, supported by the other three. E-E-A-T is not a single score or setting. It describes the signals that make content believable: real first-hand experience, accurate knowledge, a reputation others recognize, and transparent, honest information about who is behind the business.
Why E-E-A-T Matters for Northern Indiana & Michiana Businesses

Why E-E-A-T Matters for Northern Indiana & Michiana Businesses Customers in Northern Indiana choose businesses they trust, and Google tries to reward the same thing. A Kokomo roofing company that shows its owner's years on the job, real project photos, licenses, and local reviews gives both people and search engines reasons to believe it. AI tools also lean on trust signals when picking sources to cite. Clear authorship, credentials, and consistent reputation across the web make your business a safer recommendation.

How E-E-A-T Works Experience Show first-hand work: project photos, case examples, and details only someone who did the job would know. Expertise Explain topics accurately and in depth, with credentials, certifications, and training noted where relevant. Authoritativeness Earn mentions, links, reviews, and recognition from respected local and industry sources. Trustworthiness Share clear contact details, policies, pricing approach, real reviews, and accurate information.

A Local Example A Goshen financial planner rewrites her retirement planning page. She adds her credentials and years of experience, an author bio with a photo, examples of common situations her clients face, links to her regulatory listing, and recent client reviews. The page now reads like advice from a real local expert, and it begins ranking for retirement planning searches in Elkhart County.

Getting Started With E-E-A-T Start with an honest review of your website through a new customer's eyes. Can they tell who owns the business, how long you have served the area, what qualifications your team holds, and how to reach you? Every unanswered question is a trust gap to close. Next, add an About page with real names, photos, and backgrounds, and give helpful articles a named author with a short bio. Feature project photos and specific examples from jobs in towns you serve, such as Goshen, Warsaw, or South Bend. Link to your Google reviews, licenses, certifications, and association memberships. Finally, plan a few pieces of content each quarter that answer customer questions in depth, written by the people on your team who do the work every day.
Quick Wins to Improve Your E-E-A-T Signals

Quick Wins to Improve Your E-E-A-T Signals Add author bios with photos, credentials, and real experience Show real project photos and specific examples from local work Display reviews and link to your Google Business Profile Publish clear contact details, licenses, and policies Cite reputable sources when sharing statistics

What to Watch For Your-money topics. Health, finance, legal, and safety topics receive the highest scrutiny. Authentic proof. Use real photos and real reviews; stock images add little trust. Consistency. Credentials and claims should match across your site, profiles, and directories. Freshness. Update pages when facts, prices, or regulations change.

E-E-A-T FAQ Is E-E-A-T a ranking factor? Google describes E-E-A-T as a framework its systems aim to reward rather than one direct ranking factor. The signals behind it, such as reputation and helpful content, shape rankings. Why was Experience added? Google added the extra E in late 2022 to recognize the value of first-hand experience, such as having actually used a product or done the work. Do reviews affect E-E-A-T? Reviews are one of the clearest public signals of trust. A steady flow of genuine reviews, with thoughtful replies from the owner, shows both customers and search engines that real people value your work. How can a small business show authority? Earn local press, chamber and association memberships, partner links, and steady reviews, and publish genuinely helpful content about your specialty. t: What Is Entity SEO? Helping Google Understand Your Business
d: Entity SEO helps search engines and AI recognize your business as a distinct, trusted entity with clear facts and connections. Learn how local businesses build it.
s: Entity SEO Making your business a clear, recognized entity to search engines and AI

Entity SEO Making your business a clear, recognized entity to search engines and AI Entity SEO: Helping search engines and AI understand your business as a specific, real thing, with clear facts about who you are, what you do, and where you serve.

What Is Entity SEO? Entity SEO is the practice of helping search engines and AI systems understand your business as a specific "thing," known as an entity, with clear attributes and relationships. An entity has a name, a type, a location, services, people, and connections to other entities such as towns, industries, and organizations. Google organizes much of its knowledge in the Knowledge Graph, a large database of entities and how they relate. When Google confidently recognizes your business as an entity, it can show knowledge panels, connect your business to relevant searches, and give AI tools accurate facts.
Why Entity SEO Matters for Northern Indiana & Michiana Businesses

Why Entity SEO Matters for Northern Indiana & Michiana Businesses Search has moved from matching words to understanding meaning. When someone asks "Who does commercial roofing near Elkhart?", Google and AI tools look for entities known to offer commercial roofing in that area. Businesses with clear, consistent entity signals are easier to recommend. Strong entity signals also protect your brand. They help search engines separate your business from others with similar names and keep facts such as hours, owners, and services accurate across search and AI answers.

How Entity SEO Works Consistent identity Your name, address, phone, and description match everywhere. Structured data Organization and LocalBusiness schema describe your business, with sameAs links to your official profiles. Clear connections Pages link your business to services, towns, people, and associations. Authoritative mentions Chambers, news sites, associations, and directories confirm your identity. Topical depth Content that thoroughly covers your specialty strengthens what you are known for.

A Local Example Two Goshen companies share similar names, and Google often mixes up their reviews and hours. One of them adds Organization and LocalBusiness schema with sameAs links to its Google Business Profile, Facebook, LinkedIn, and BBB listing, updates every directory with consistent details, and publishes an About page naming its founder and history. Google begins showing an accurate knowledge panel, and AI tools describe the company correctly. The company also earns a feature in a local business journal, which adds another trusted source confirming its identity and specialty.

Getting Started With Entity SEO Search your business name on Google and in a few AI tools. Note whether a knowledge panel appears, whether the facts are correct, and whether any information belongs to a different business. Then strengthen your entity signals. Write a clear About page, add Organization and LocalBusiness schema with sameAs links to your official profiles, make your details consistent across directories, and link to the people, services, and towns that define your business. Over time, earn mentions from trusted local and industry sources.
Quick Wins to Improve Your Entity Signals

Quick Wins to Improve Your Entity Signals Write a detailed About page with your history and team Add Organization schema with sameAs links to official profiles Keep your business details identical across the web Create pages for each core service and service area Earn mentions from local associations and media

What to Watch For Name confusion. Similar business names require especially consistent signals. Outdated profiles. Old directory listings can confuse search engines. Thin About pages. Detailed, factual information helps machines and people. Patience. Entity recognition grows gradually as signals add up.

Entity SEO FAQ What is an entity in SEO? A distinct, identifiable thing, such as a business, person, place, or product, that search engines can understand and connect to other things. How do I get a Google knowledge panel? Panels appear when Google confidently recognizes an entity. Consistent details, structured data, and trusted mentions help. Does entity SEO help with AI search? Yes. AI tools rely on clear, consistent facts about entities to give accurate recommendations. What are sameAs links? Schema properties that point to your official profiles elsewhere, helping search engines connect them to your business. Put It to Work Want Google and AI tools to know exactly who your business is? t: What Is a Google Business Profile? A Local Business Guide
d: Learn what a Google Business Profile is, how it ranks in Google Maps, and the steps Northern Indiana and Michiana businesses take to turn their profile into calls.
s: Google Business Profile The free Google listing that puts your business on Maps and in local search

Google Business Profile The free Google listing that puts your business on Maps and in local search Google Business Profile: Your free listing on Google Search and Google Maps. It shows your hours, phone number, photos, services, and customer reviews.

What Is Google Business Profile? A Google Business Profile is the free listing Google shows when someone searches for your business by name or looks for a service near them. It holds the details a customer needs to choose you: your name, hours, phone number, website, address or service area, photos, services, products, posts, and reviews. It appears on Google Search, in the map pack, and inside Google Maps. For most local businesses, the profile is the first impression. Many customers read your reviews, check your hours, look at photos, and tap to call without ever visiting your website. That makes the profile a working storefront, and Google treats it as one of the strongest signals for where you show up in local results.
Why Google Business Profile Matters for Northern Indiana & Michiana Businesses

Why Google Business Profile Matters for Northern Indiana & Michiana Businesses In towns like Goshen, Elkhart, Warsaw, and South Bend, people search with a location in mind: "plumber near me," "best pizza in Mishawaka," "dentist open Saturday." Google answers those searches with profiles, and the businesses with complete, active, well-reviewed profiles earn the clicks and calls. A strong profile also feeds AI tools. Google AI Overviews, Gemini, and other assistants pull business facts from profiles and reviews, so accurate categories, services, and hours help AI describe your business correctly when customers ask for recommendations.

How Google Business Profile Works Claim and verify Google confirms you own the business, usually through a postcard, phone, email, or video check. Fill in every field Primary category, secondary categories, services, hours, attributes, description, and service area all tell Google which searches you fit. Earn and answer reviews Review count, rating, recency, and your replies shape both rankings and trust. Stay active Photos, posts, product updates, and answered questions show Google and customers that the business is open and engaged. Measure results The Performance tab shows searches, calls, direction requests, and website clicks so you see what the profile produces.

A Local Example A family HVAC company in Elkhart County switches its primary category from "Contractor" to "HVAC Contractor," adds furnace repair, AC installation, and duct cleaning as services, uploads job photos every week, and asks every happy customer for a review with a short link. Within a few months the company appears in the map pack for "furnace repair Goshen " and calls from the profile climb, which the owner tracks in the Performance tab.
Getting Started With Google Business Profile

Getting Started With Google Business Profile Start by searching your business name on Google and Google Maps. If a profile appears, select "Own this business?" to claim it. If none appears, create one at business.google.com using your exact business name, the category that best describes your main service, and your phone number and website. Once verified, set aside an hour to complete every section. Write a description that explains who you serve and which towns you cover, such as Elkhart, Goshen, and Middlebury. Add at least ten real photos, including your team, your work, your vehicles, and your location. Then build a simple weekly habit: one new photo or post, a reply to every new review, and a quick check of your hours. Small, steady activity adds up faster than a single big update once a year.
Quick Wins to Improve Your Google Business Profile

Quick Wins to Improve Your Google Business Profile Choose the most specific primary category that matches your main service List every service with a short description that uses the words customers search Add fresh, real photos of your team, work, and location each month Reply to every review, thanking happy customers and helping unhappy ones Keep holiday and seasonal hours current so customers always see accurate times

What to Watch For Matching details. Keep your name, address, and phone number identical on your profile, website, and directories so Google trusts your location. Real business name. Use your actual business name; keyword-stuffed names can lead to suspension. Service areas. Service-area businesses can hide their street address and list the towns they serve instead. Review requests. Ask every customer the same way; offering rewards for reviews breaks Google policy.

Google Business Profile FAQ Is a Google Business Profile free? Yes. Creating and managing a Google Business Profile is free. Most businesses see movement within a few weeks of completing the profile, with steady gains over several months as reviews, photos, and posts add up. Do I need a storefront to have a profile? No. Service-area businesses such as plumbers, cleaners, and contractors can create a profile, hide their address, and list the areas they serve. t: What Is Google Search Console? A Free SEO Tool Explained

s: Google Search Console Google's free dashboard for your website's search performance

Google Search Console Google's free dashboard for your website's search performance Google Search Console: A free Google tool that shows which searches bring people to your site, how often your pages appear, and which pages Google has stored.

What Is Google Search Console? Google Search Console is a free tool from Google that shows how your website appears in Google search results. It reports the searches that show your pages, how many clicks and impressions each page earns, and whether Google can crawl and index your site. It also alerts you to problems such as indexing errors, mobile usability issues, Core Web Vitals scores, security issues, and manual actions. You verify ownership of your site once and then access reports anytime.
Why Google Search Console Matters for Northern Indiana & Michiana Businesses

Why Google Search Console Matters for Northern Indiana & Michiana Businesses Search Console is the clearest window into how Google sees your website. A Mishawaka dentist can see that people searching "emergency dentist near me" are finding its pages, which pages earn the most clicks, and which pages Google has not indexed. Because it is free and comes directly from Google, it is one of the most valuable tools for any Northern Indiana business investing in SEO. It also gives you proof. When you update a page or publish new content, Search Console shows whether impressions and clicks actually grew, so you can see which efforts pay off and explain results to partners or staff with real numbers instead of impressions.

How Google Search Console Works Performance report Shows queries, clicks, impressions, click-through rate, and average position. Pages report Lists which pages are indexed and why others are not. URL inspection Checks any page's index status and lets you request indexing. Sitemaps Submit your sitemap and monitor discovered pages. Experience reports Core Web Vitals and HTTPS status show page experience.

A Local Example A Valparaiso landscaping company checks Search Console and finds that its "patio installation" page appears in thousands of searches each month yet earns few clicks, with an average position on the second page. It improves the page's title tag, expands the content with photos and pricing ranges, and adds internal links from related pages. Within a few months, the page moves onto the first page and clicks rise. The Pages report also reveals several old service pages that were never indexed, which the company updates and adds to its sitemap.
Getting Started With Google Search Console

Getting Started With Google Search Console Sign in at search.google.com/search-console with a Google account and add your website. Verify ownership using the method your website platform supports, such as a DNS record or HTML tag, and submit your XML sitemap. Once data appears, spend fifteen minutes each month in three reports. Use Performance to see top queries and pages, Pages to find indexing problems, and Core Web Vitals to check page experience. Look for pages with high impressions and low clicks, since those are often your fastest wins.
Quick Wins to Improve Your Search Console Insights

Quick Wins to Improve Your Search Console Insights Verify your site and submit your sitemap Review top queries and pages monthly Find high-impression, low-click pages to improve Check the Pages report for indexing problems Request indexing after publishing important pages

What to Watch For Data delay. Reports update with a short delay, so recent changes take a few days to appear. Average position. It averages many searches and locations; use it as a trend. Ownership access. Keep access under your own Google account and add partners as users. Alerts. Read emails from Search Console, since they flag important issues.

Google Search Console FAQ Is Google Search Console free? Yes. It is completely free for any website owner. What is the difference between Search Console and Google Analytics? Search Console shows how people find you in Google search. Google Analytics shows what visitors do once they reach your site. How long does data take to appear? Data typically begins appearing within a few days of verification. Can I see local search data? Search Console shows queries and country data. Google Business Profile shows map and local profile activity. Who should own the account? Your business should own the property, with your marketing partner added as a user. t: What Is an Internal Link? How Linking Your Pages Helps SEO
d: Internal links connect pages on your own website. Learn how they guide visitors, spread authority, and help Google understand your services and service areas.
s: Internal Link Links between your own pages that guide visitors and search engines

Internal Link Links between your own pages that guide visitors and search engines Internal Link: A link from one page on your website to another page on the same website. Internal links guide visitors to helpful pages and show search engines how your content connects.

What Is Internal Link? An internal link is a link from one page on your website to another page on the same site. Navigation menus, footer links, buttons, and links inside paragraphs are all internal links. Internal links do three jobs at once. They help visitors find related information, they help search engines discover and understand your pages, and they pass authority from strong pages to the pages you most want to rank.
Why Internal Link Matters for Northern Indiana & Michiana Businesses

Why Internal Link Matters for Northern Indiana & Michiana Businesses Many local business websites have great service pages that search engines rarely visit because nothing links to them. An Elkhart County roofer whose blog post on hail damage links directly to its "Storm Damage Roof Repair" page sends both readers and ranking signals where they matter most. Internal links also tell a clear story about your expertise. Linking related services, town pages, and helpful guides together shows Google and AI tools that your business covers a topic thoroughly across Northern Indiana and Michiana.

How Internal Link Works Discovery Search engines follow links to find new and updated pages. Context The linked words, called anchor text, describe the page being linked. Authority flow Pages with strong rankings or backlinks share value with the pages they link to. Structure Linking patterns show which pages are most important and how topics relate. Visitor paths Clear links move readers from questions to services to contact.

A Local Example A Valparaiso landscaping company publishes a guide to spring lawn care. It adds links inside the article to its lawn aeration, fertilization, and landscape design service pages, plus its Porter County service area page. Each service page links back to related guides. The service pages begin ranking higher, and visitors who arrive on the guide more often request a quote.

Getting Started With Internal Link List your most important pages: the services that bring in the most revenue and the towns you most want to serve. Then search your site for articles, FAQs, and other pages that mention those topics without linking to them. Each mention is a ready-made internal link opportunity. Add links using descriptive words such as "furnace repair in Goshen " rather than "click here." Make sure every important page receives links from several related pages and is reachable within a few clicks from the homepage. Repeat the review whenever you publish new content so each new page connects to the rest of your site right away.
Quick Wins to Improve Your Internal Linking

Quick Wins to Improve Your Internal Linking Link every blog post to at least one related service page Use descriptive anchor text that names the destination topic Link service pages to the towns and counties you serve Add related links at the end of articles and service pages Fix or remove links to pages that no longer exist

What to Watch For Orphan pages. Pages with no internal links are hard for search engines and visitors to find. Generic anchors. "Click here" tells search engines nothing about the destination. Broken links. Update links after changing URLs so visitors never hit dead ends. Relevance. Link where it genuinely helps the reader take the next step.

Internal Link FAQ How many internal links should a page have? There is no fixed number. Add links wherever they help readers, and make sure every important page receives several relevant links. Do footer and menu links count? Yes. They help discovery, while links inside the main content carry stronger context about the destination. Are internal links as valuable as backlinks? They work differently. Backlinks bring authority from outside, and internal links share and direct that authority within your site. Should I link to the same page more than once? One clear link per page is usually enough; repeated links add little extra value. Put It to Work Want your website working as one connected system?
